fragments.text: Every room I told you about had an audience. The hotel lobby. The theatre seats. The parlor at the Inn. The village is not a collection of buildings — it is a collection of gatherings waiting to happen again.

Five buildings. Twelve-inch brick walls, old-growth timber, a foundation set during the railroad era that has not moved in a century. The material facts argue for preservation. The material facts always win.
I have passed through here more times than I can count. On the train, in a car, on foot. Every time, Dunsmuir looked like a place that was almost something. This time, I am staying.
